There is a magic in the blue hour, where night surrenders but day hasn't fully claimed the throne. I sit by the window, watching the gradient shift from inky black to deep purple, and finally to soft gold. It happens every day, yet I rarely witness it in full, as the alarm interrupts the ceremony.

In this suspended time, the world feels quieter, almost hushed, as if the earth takes a deep breath before the noise begins. No notifications, no urgent demands. Just a distant siren fading and wind rustling through the tall oak trees outside. Everything happening today is merely an abstract idea in this quiet space. It is a gift.

We rush through transitions in modern life. We check phones before our feet touch the floor, we swallow coffee before tasting the fresh air. We treat the morning as a task, a checklist of obligations rather than a threshold. But standing here, I truly remember light is the first teacher. It arrives without judgment and illuminates whatever is there.

The day is waiting, but for now, I stay in the blue. It is a rebellion against the rush, a pocket of stillness in a chaotic world. When the sun crests the roof, I'll step out. But until then, I am content with the light that isn't quite there yet, holding space for the silence.
